tests.Test Description: Validates default reset values and masked write/read behavior across per-pin and group GPIO configuration/status registers using 32-bit register accesses. The test iterates a fixed register list, skips non-readable/writable entries per masks, and compares read data against expected default or computed values based on write/read masks.
tests.Remarks: Certain registers are intentionally skipped during default-value and write/read checks as indicated by the skip arrays. A note in definitions indicates that reading default values of input data registers may show high if no external drive is forced; clearing or forcing input can affect bit-level selection and expected values.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: invoke the test entry function for this case.
Perform default-value checks across the defined register list for pins 8 through 39 and the specified group registers, skipping those marked as non-readable or excluded.
For each of six predefined 32-bit data patterns, apply masked writes to all writable registers in the list while skipping the excluded ones.
For each register written, perform a masked read and compute the expected value using the read mask and write mask combined with the default value for non-writable bits.
Compare the read value to the expected value for each register and pattern; log mismatches and accumulate failure counters.
Conclude the test by reporting pass if no default-value or write/read mismatches were detected; otherwise report failure.

tests.Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input.
tests.Test Description: Exercises negative-edge interrupt detection for GPIO pins 8 through 39 using interrupt routing through system registers and GIC. Each pin is configured for input and negative-edge detection, a falling edge is generated, and the handler validates per-pin status, group status, raw clear, and system interrupt clear.
tests.Remarks: The test conditionally targets one of two GPIO interrupt lines depending on compile-time selection and uses bounded waits to avoid infinite loops. The handler returns the pad driver to a known state after servicing to avoid spurious events.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: invoke the test entry function for this case.
Enable the appropriate interrupt line in the interrupt controller.
Enable the corresponding system interrupt output for the selected GPIO block.
Initialize the external drive to a known high level at the referenced address.
Configure pins 8 through 39 for input mode and negative-edge detection, and clear any per-pin raw status; include a short delay between configurations.
For each pin from 8 through 39: clear the corresponding raw group status bit; enable only this pin in the group enable; include a short delay.
For each enabled pin, arm the wait for an interrupt before generating an input transition.
Drive the external bus high, delay, then drive the bit low to create a falling edge on exactly that pin.
Wait for the interrupt condition to be serviced within a bounded timeout; if the timeout expires, record an error and continue.

On interrupt service: restore the external drive to all-high, read the per-pin control/status, confirm input low after falling edge, confirm the bit is set in the group masked status, clear per-pin raw and group raw status, recheck that the group status is cleared, clear the system raw status, and clear the interrupt controller pending state.
Complete iterations for all pins and report the aggregated result.

tests.Test Description: Enables positive-edge detection for all GPIO pins 8 through 39, configures group IO control to input mode, enables group interrupts, and then generates a rising edge per pin. The interrupt handler validates that group status is raised, clears per-pin raw status for all pins, verifies group status clears, and clears system interrupt status.
tests.Remarks: Interrupt service temporarily masks the group enable while handling, clears per-pin raw status for all pins, then re-enables the group at the end. The main loop arms the wait before generating the edge to avoid race conditions.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: invoke the test entry function for this case.
Enable the appropriate interrupt line in the interrupt controller.
Enable the corresponding system interrupt output for the selected GPIO block.
For pins 8 through 39, enable positive-edge detection at each per-pin control register.
Configure group IO control registers to set pins 8 through 39 to input mode.
Enable all bits in the group interrupt enable register.
For each pin from 8 through 39: drive the external bus low, delay, arm the wait for the interrupt, then drive high to create a rising edge.
For each event, wait for the handler to service the interrupt within a bounded timeout; on timeout, record an error and break.

In the handler: read group masked status, temporarily mask group enables, confirm status is nonzero, clear per-pin raw status across all pins, confirm group status is cleared, clear system interrupt status, and re-enable group interrupt before clearing the interrupt controller pending state.
Complete iterations and report the aggregated result.
